name: FFmpeg Alphamerge Alpha Mask Pipeline
use_when: A rendered text, glow, lower-third, or graphic foreground needs to be revealed through a grayscale mask.
The agent needs a reusable transparent foreground before final overlay.
A CapCut-style split mask, shine sweep, or highlight wipe must be reproduced in FFmpeg.
avoid_when: The goal is direct weighted blending between two opaque sources; use maskedmerge instead.
The foreground and mask dimensions, fps, or duration are not aligned.
A simple NLE mask or Remotion CSS mask would be clearer and easier to debug.
The final output format will strip alpha before the overlay is used.

timeline_pattern.pattern: foreground_render -> grayscale_mask -> format_alignment -> alphamerge -> overlay_or_alpha_export -> contact_sheet_qc
timeline_pattern.polarity_rule: White/high mask values reveal the foreground; black/low values hide it.
timeline_pattern.format_rule: Use explicit format steps when necessary so alpha is preserved and interpreted correctly.

motion.rule: Animated masks must be generated with the same resolution, fps, duration, and intended timing as the foreground.

keyframe_values.short_text_wipe: 6-15 frames at 30 fps for fast text reveals.
keyframe_values.lower_third_wipe: 12-24 frames at 30 fps for calmer overlay reveals.
keyframe_values.mask_preview: Preview at least reveal start, midpoint, final visible hold, and clear frames.

sound.rule: If used, SFX should land on the visible reveal frame, not the start of the mask file, and remain below dialogue.

captions.rule: Keep captions away from the masked overlay region unless the overlay replaces those captions.

color.rule: Inspect semi-transparent mask edges over contrasting backgrounds for dark halos, premultiply issues, or muddy glow.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use [foreground][mask]alphamerge[foreground_alpha]; then [background][foreground_alpha]overlay=format=auto[final], or export foreground_alpha to an alpha-capable format.
implementation.remotion: Equivalent logic is duplicate/styled layers revealed by CSS masks; export the result as transparent overlay if FFmpeg will composite later.
implementation.blender: Use grayscale masks as compositor alpha inputs for a foreground layer, then composite or export with alpha.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use Split/Film Strip masks on duplicated/compounded foreground layers; verify start/end outside the word.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use track mattes or masked nested graphics to reveal a foreground layer above the base.

common_mistakes: Expecting overlay alone to create a mask reveal.
Using a mask with the wrong polarity.
Letting mask and foreground frame properties mismatch.
Converting to a non-alpha pixel format before alpha is needed.
Reusing graph labels ambiguously and merging the wrong stream.
qc: Mask preview shows correct polarity and edge softness.
Foreground and mask match width, height, fps, duration, and timing.
Alpha survives until the intended final overlay or alpha export step.
Start/mid/hold/clear contact frames show no black rectangle or sliver.
Final render has no unintended caption, face, proof, UI, product, or action overlap.
